title: sfx_fixture doesn't match the harness/growth.dem fixture; its seed pipe draw is silently rejected (span 23 > max_span 14)
detail: The test fixture's three nodes sit at different positions than the real harness fixture, so its seed draw spans 23 tiles and is silently rejected — every shadow-exactness pin runs on a topology no demo produces, while the comment claims the demo's exact recipe.
recommended_fix: Use the harness fixture positions ({8,15},{20,15},{32,15}) so draw 1→3 spans 14 (legal) and matches growth.dem — or rewrite the comment to stop claiming the demo's recipe; check the apply_edit result.

title: spawn_fx_init / spawn_fx_destroy still have zero call sites (r1 flag unfixed)
evidence: app/render/spawn_fx.odin:92: "spawn_fx_init :: proc(fx: ^Spawn_FX, allocator := context.allocator) {" and :97: "spawn_fx_destroy :: proc(fx: ^Spawn_FX) {" — a repo-wide grep across app/, harness/, core/ for `spawn_fx_init|spawn_fx_destroy` matches only these two definitions; the harness uses rnd.spawn_fx_reset (harness/run.odin:293: "rnd.spawn_fx_reset(&rc.view.spawn_fx)") and the app rnd.spawn_fx_reset (app/main.odin:741), never init/destroy.
detail: Both procs are dead code (r1 flagged; still dead at r4). Spawn_FX.reveals instead grows on the ambient allocator at first append — works here (bounded ≤4 entries, long-lived View), but the pair is unreferenced.
recommended_fix: Delete spawn_fx_init/spawn_fx_destroy, or call init from View setup and destroy at teardown so `reveals` has an explicit owner and allocator.

title: sfx_load_cat's allocator parameter is still unused (r1 flag unfixed)
evidence: app/render/spawn_fx_test.odin:36: "sfx_load_cat :: proc(cat: ^pp.Catalogs, allocator := context.allocator) {" — but the body never references `allocator`: read1 allocates via "b, err := os.read_entire_file_from_path(path, context.allocator)" and the load call is "if e := pp.catalogs_load(cat, &src); e.file != "" {" with no allocator argument; callers pass it anyway, e.g. :112 "sfx_load_cat(&cat, context.temp_allocator)".
detail: The parameter is declared and passed by every caller but ignored — file bytes and catalog arrays allocate on the ambient context.allocator regardless. r1 flagged this; it is still unfixed.
recommended_fix: Drop the unused `allocator` parameter from sfx_load_cat (callers pass only &cat), or thread it into read1 and catalogs_load.
